title: Serpentshrine Cavern
body: Serpentshrine Cavern is the deepest hold of Coilfang Reservoir, a vast flooded cavern beneath Serpent Lake and the seat of Lady Vashj, matron of the Coilfang naga. Here the water drawn in from the bogs gathers, and the work never stops: Vashj'ir honor guards drive their workers at the pumps and valves, boasting that the reservoir fills nicely and that soon all of Draenor's water will be theirs. Coilfang priestesses, shatterers, serpentguards and fathom-witches walk its halls, Greyheart Broken serve the naga as technicians, tidecallers and nether-mages, Tidewalker murlocs crowd one shore, and colossi of the bog and sporebats roam the wilder reaches. Frenzies swarm the dark water. Her lords hold the cavern's outer chambers, and Vashj herself waits at its heart.
sources: zones/serpentshrine_cavern.txt (map 548: area 3607 only)

title: Hydross the Unstable
body: Hydross the Unstable, called the Duke of Currents, is a great lord of water who dwells in a chamber of Serpentshrine Cavern. Tainted water spirits come to him one after another, and he purifies them and sends them on clean. Yet his name is earned. He tells intruders that he cannot allow them to interfere, and when he is drawn out of the cleansing field about him, the poison takes him at once: he cries out in pain and turns foul. Drawn back in, he grows clean, sighing that this is better, much better.

parts.body: Hydross fell in his chamber, and his last words depended on what he was when he died. Pure, he sighed that he was released. Poisoned, he turned on his killers with an accusation: they were the disease, not he. Either way, the Duke of Currents was no more.

title: The Lurker Below
body: At the center of Serpentshrine Cavern lies a strange pool, its water dark and still, and something lives beneath it that does not show itself to the idle. Only one who casts a line into the pool may draw it up: the Lurker Below, a great beast of the deep that surfaces in a rush of water. It spouts torrents across those who stand against it, lashes about in a whirling frenzy and bursts geysers beneath their feet, and when it dives again, Coilfang ambushers and guardians rise from the depths to fight in its place.

parts.body: The Lurker Below died in its pool. With it went the danger of the cavern's water: after its fall the frenzies no longer swarmed about those who swam, and the water of Serpentshrine could be crossed in peace.

title: Leotheras the Blind
body: Leotheras the Blind is a blood elf demon hunter, and he is a prisoner in Serpentshrine Cavern. Three Greyheart spellbinders keep him banished, kneeling and helpless within their spells, and only when the last of them falls is he free. Finally, he cries, his banishment ends. He fights with twin blades, spinning in a whirlwind of steel, but he is not alone in his body. From time to time a demon takes him over, mocking the trifling elf it has cast aside, wearing a fiend's shape and whispering to his foes that we all have our demons.

parts.body: Near the end the elf took back his body, but the struggle broke him: no, he cried, he was the master, and he could not contain him. His demon tore free as a shadow of its own, rejoicing that it was liberated at last, and the two fought on side by side until Leotheras fell, and his shadow vanished with him.

title: Fathom-Lord Karathress
body: Fathom-Lord Karathress is a naga lord of Serpentshrine Cavern, and he holds his chamber with three Fathom-Guards at his side: Sharkkis, a hunter with beasts at his call, Tidalvess, a shaman of totems and frost, and Caribdis, a caster of water and cyclones who mends her allies' wounds. When intruders come he calls his guards to attention, for they have visitors, and he hurls bolts and searing novas at those who dare his hall. In a cage at the edge of his chamber sits a prisoner, a Broken called Seer Olum.

parts.body: As each of the Fathom-Guards fell, its power passed to its lord, but Karathress could not hold his hall. When the fathom-lord died, the cage at the edge of his chamber swung open, and its prisoner, Seer Olum, walked free.

title: Morogrim Tidewalker
body: Morogrim Tidewalker is a giant of the sea who rules a shore of Serpentshrine Cavern, where the Tidewalker murlocs who bear his name crowd about the water: warriors, shamans, harpooners, hydromancers and depth-seers. He greets intruders with a curse, flood of the deep take you, and fights with the sea itself, hurling tidal waves, sealing foes in watery graves and shaking the ground with earthquakes. When the earth shakes the murlocs come running from the shallows, and he calls on his subjects to destroy his foes.

parts.body: As he weakened the Tidewalker sent globules of water to hunt his foes instead of graves, but he fell all the same on the shore he ruled. His last words meant nothing to those who heard them: great currents of Ageon.
sources: creature_text 21213 group 4 (Great currents of... Ageon...)

title: Lady Vashj
body: Lady Vashj is the matron of the Coilfang naga and the mistress of Serpentshrine Cavern. Long ago she was one of the Highborne of ancient Kalimdor, a handmaiden to Queen Azshara, and she rose from the sea with her naga when Illidan Stormrage called on them; she has served him ever since, and followed him to Outland. Throughout Coilfang her naga cry that Illidan reigns. To any who reach her she declares her purpose: water is life, a rare commodity in Outland that her people alone shall control, and the time has come at last for the Highborne to retake their rightful place in the world.

parts.body: Vashj fought with bow and lightning, then drew back to the heart of her platform behind a barrier fed by four shield generators, calling elementals, elite naga and striders against her foes. When the barrier fell she came on again under clouds of toxic sporebats. At the last she died with an apology to her master: Lord Illidan, I am sorry.
sources: creature_text 21212 group 7 (Lord Illidan, I... I am... sorry.)
